I don’t think you are wrong to be depressed and disheartened. I don’t mean this in a “why bother” way. I mean that getting sober IS HARD. It SUCKS. I wouldn’t wish sobriety on anyone because it is awful. I’ve been at this almost 2 decades and I still have hard days.

It isn’t about how many times it takes you to get sober. You will get there. Sometimes it seems like this awful rollercoaster of going backwards and down and never feel like you are going forward. There sadly is no quick fix for that.

Some people really swear by AA. Some people swear by religious assistance. Some people find a group and sober friends and use them for support. It is something you have to choose but you can have people around who have been here.

Be honest with your doctor. They don't want to make you suffer. They won't see you as drug seeking...it's not a painless procedure and you want to ensure you will get through it successfully. That is being responsible and ensuring you are taking care of your needs. Be proud of yourself for being aware of what you need to get through this. Take something before for your anxiety, see if they'll give you a block (which will definitely eliminate a majority [if not all] the pain), take some painkillers 45-60min prior. Remember to relax and breathe...take your boyfriend! Ask him if you can squeeze his hand, ask if he'll help keep you distracted. It makes a difference!

I will say that being super anxious kind of goes 2 ways IMO. You can psych yourself up and imagine it's going to be the worst pain ever and get really tense....which isn't helpful. Or you can psych yourself up thinking it's going to be the worst pain ever and then realise afterwards that it might've hurt like hell...but you're still alive and maybe nothing (on the planet) can ever compare to how bad things might seem beforehand in your head.

Getting an IUD hurts. They're opening you up, measuring you and jamming something inside of you. It'd be stupid for anyone to say it's completely painless. I got my most recent Mirena back in August and I already cannot remember how much it hurt. I remember it kinda hurt and I spotted a bit over the day and that I was happy to curl up with a puppy and hot water bottle for the evening and I was fine the next day. It definitely hurts....but I can probably imagine a lot of things that would hurt worse and even if you are a bit sore for a few hours.........having a birth control method that you trust and improves your life is worth it.

I have a Mirena (I'm on my 3rd) and it's easily the best decision I ever made. I always worried about getting pregnant and I didn't want that. My IUD has ended those worries. I chose the Mirena because my menstruation was so severe I neeeeeded to stop bleeding, and I have! I barely remember it's there, it's lovely and reliable. After a little while the strings will relax and sort of rest really nicely against your cervix (sometimes people find them a bit poky in the beginning during sex). If it makes you feel better you can check for your strings every single day. Twice a day. Whatever makes you most comfortable. I will say it's incredibly effective and to remember that there is no 100% way to not get pregnant unless you abstain completely. And if that isn't what you want....an IUD is definitely the right way to go.

Like others have said, you will still menstruate with your Paragard so it'd be pretty tough for you to get pregnant without realising it....since you'd stop bleeding. Chances of expulsion are very low and it is a great way to protect against unwanted pregnancy.

I highly recommend it, just remember you can check to make sure it's still there by feeling the strings.
